threats.title: The discovery source is unavailable, throttled or reindexed
threats.threat: Lumeus Activity or RPC answers 429 or 5xx, asks to wait until a daily cap resets, times out on a heavy window, rebuilds its index under a new generation, or puts arbitrary codes and error text in its answers.
threats.stellar: Discovery reads history by ledger range; a testnet reset also changes the generation and starts ledger numbers again.
threats.preconditions: Any outage, rate limit or index rebuild of the discovery source.
threats.impact: Without protection: a stalled or crashing indexer, hammering a throttled service, or a walk stitched from two read views.

mitigations.text: 429 and 5xx answers are retried a bounded number of times after Retry-After; a Retry-After over 60 s stops the walk instead of waiting; query_timeout is never repeated unchanged (the window narrows and resumes after the last page stored); generation_changed restarts there without the old read view.
A transient discovery failure keeps the route's checkpoint and is retried in the next round (after the Retry-After the source asked for); the report and health show the lag meanwhile.
Ledger reads through Lumeus RPC follow Retry-After too, never wait more than 60 s, and a longer one pauses every ledger read until then instead of retrying each round.
Metric labels for Lumeus failures come from a fixed set of documented codes (anything else is other), and health shows only the stable code of a stop, never remote error text.

A candidate whose bytes or anchor are not available yet waits (15 s, doubling, at most an hour) without holding back newer candidates, and anchors are read in Horizon /ledgers pages for runs of nearby ledgers; the report still stops before a waiting ledger.

At the head, channel and settlement-authority routes, which Lumeus lists only when they pay a fee or move funds, are walked every EXPLORER_SLOW_ROUTE_ROUNDS rounds instead of every round, bounding empty polls (billed on mainnet).

threats.title: A payer named for a transfer it never authorized
threats.threat: Someone deploys a token whose transfer never calls from.require_auth() and lands a sponsored transfer whose one authorization entry names a chosen account, unsigned or with a signature that does not verify, so that the Explorer shows that account paying a chosen seller.
threats.stellar: The host authenticates an address authorization entry, and consumes its nonce, only when a contract calls require_auth for that address; no check covers entries that no contract asked for. A Stellar Asset Contract's transfer always calls from.require_auth(); any other token's own code decides.
threats.preconditions: Any account that can deploy a token contract and pay a transaction fee. An indexed row also needs its ledger read (a registered facilitator relaying it, or registry activity in the same ledger); a live lookup reads it directly.
threats.impact: Without protection: an arbitrary account shown as the payer on its account page, the payment page and the API and, through a facilitator that relays any asset, counted in the headline payments and distinct payers.

mitigations.text: R-EXACT names a payer only when consensus-bound data proves its authorization (check E7): the token is a verified Stellar Asset Contract, or the payer's own key signed the entry; anything else is excluded as unproven_authorization, and E3 and E4 describe only the entry's fields.

The signature check rebuilds the payload the network signs (the HashIdPreimage of Address or AddressV2 credentials on this network), requires the form the network checks for an account (1 to 20 signatures, strictly ascending keys) with the payer's own key among them and an expiration ledger not before the transaction's, verifies that key's signature only (one check per transfer, whatever the entry carries), and never proves a contract payer.
The rules version moved to 2, and the indexer reads every ledger indexed under another rules version again when it starts, so no row of the earlier rules stays in the index.

Until then, and for epochs the indexer no longer reads, the Explorer's reads leave out rows of other rules, its account totals while the epoch holds such ledgers, and reports or network windows of other rules; a transaction of such a row is looked up and classified again.
The SDK's inspectTransaction and rail402 tx say an exact payer authorized the transfer only when a Stellar Asset Contract's transfer or the payer's own signature proves it.
